entries.label: Why are you interested in this opportunity?
entries.value: I'm interested because quality engineering is close to the problem I keep coming back to on my own: deciding whether a system should be trusted, not just whether it runs. At Intelehealth I designed an evaluation framework for AI-generated clinical outputs against a 4,169-case clinical standard, using stratified sampling to surface systematic failure modes rather than reporting a single accuracy number. On a job-application agent I built in TypeScript and Playwright, I designed an explicit validation ladder (unit confirmed, fixture confirmed, live read-only confirmed, live mutation confirmed) because a capability passing against a local fixture does not mean it works against reality, and mutating actions sat behind fail-closed flags that never default to on. That is the same instinct quality work requires. NISC's software runs the operations of 1,200+ energy cooperatives and communication organizations, so a defect is not an abstraction; it reaches utilities serving real communities. I also want to be somewhere AI is being adopted deliberately, since I care a lot about where automation should stop and human review should begin. I'd like to spend a summer testing enterprise software that people actually depend on and learning how a team at that scale defines done.
